strengths: Comprehensive coverage of humanoid robot commercialization technologies.
Clear delineation of core and boundary technologies.

technology_axes.name: Full-Body Control and Balance
technology_axes.description: Technologies enabling full-body control and balance in humanoid robots, including bipedal locomotion and whole-body dynamics.

source_refs.claim: The technology must enable full-body control and balance in humanoid robots.
Humanoid robots integrate mobility, manipulation, control, and AI into a human-like system.

technology_axes.rationale: Full-body control and balance are essential for humanoid robots to perform tasks in dynamic environments, aligning with both user query and owner documentation.
boundary_examples: Technologies for bipedal locomotion in humanoid robots.

technology_axes.name: Advanced Manipulation Capabilities
technology_axes.description: Technologies facilitating advanced manipulation capabilities, including robotic hands, grippers, and tactile sensing.

source_refs.claim: The technology must facilitate advanced manipulation capabilities, including robotic hands and tactile sensing.
Key technologies for humanoid robots include manipulation, control, and AI-based learning.

technology_axes.rationale: Advanced manipulation is critical for humanoid robots to interact with their environment effectively, supported by both user query and owner documentation.

technology_axes.name: Learning and Control of Multi-Joint Manipulation
technology_axes.description: Technologies involving learning and control of multi-joint manipulation, including motion planning and force control.

source_refs.claim: The technology must involve learning and control of multi-joint manipulation.
Learning-based grasping and manipulation, motion planning, force and impedance control are included.

technology_axes.rationale: Multi-joint manipulation is a complex task requiring advanced learning and control techniques, essential for humanoid robots.
boundary_examples: Motion planning algorithms for humanoid robots.
Force control systems for multi-joint manipulation.

technology_axes.name: Joint Actuators and Reducers
technology_axes.description: Technologies including joint actuators and reducers, such as quasi-direct drive (QDD) and series elastic actuators (SEA).

source_refs.claim: The technology must include joint actuators and reducers, such as QDD and SEA.
Joint actuators and reducers like QDD and SEA are core technologies.

technology_axes.rationale: Joint actuators and reducers are fundamental components for humanoid robot movement and control, as documented by the owner and observed in the corpus.
boundary_examples: SEA for joint flexibility and control.

technology_axes.name: Robot Vision and Imitation Learning
technology_axes.description: Technologies supporting robot vision, vision-language-action (VLA) models, and imitation learning for humanoid robots.

source_refs.claim: The technology must support robot vision, VLA, and imitation learning.
Vision-Language-Action (VLA) and End-to-End (E2E) neural networks are crucial for autonomous learning and generalization in humanoid robots.

technology_axes.rationale: Vision and imitation learning are critical for humanoid robots to perceive and learn from their environment, aligning with both user query and owner documentation.
boundary_examples: Imitation learning algorithms for robotic tasks.

technology_axes.name: Safe Human-Robot Collaboration
technology_axes.description: Technologies ensuring safe human-robot collaboration, including collision detection and avoidance, and speed and separation monitoring.

source_refs.claim: The technology must ensure safe human-robot collaboration.
Human collaboration safety, including collision detection and avoidance, is a core technology.

technology_axes.rationale: Safe collaboration is essential for humanoid robots to operate alongside humans, supported by both user query and owner documentation.
boundary_examples: Collision detection systems for humanoid robots.
